name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,231

clue.text: Manoeuvre against part of the church?

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Someone scheming against a section of their own congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the church part is a building feature, not a faction of worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot or scheme secretly together is to work an angle, so both verbs describe underhand tactical moves.

clue.text: Drink companies finish off Coca-Cola

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, and two companies give it twice
the brand name ends in this letter

explanation.surface: Beverage firms getting the better of the soft-drink giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' reads as defeating the rival brand, but it only asks for the last letter of Coca-Cola.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: Travelling in an RV around America is bliss

indicators.note: things that are travelling are on the move, so the letters shift into a new order
to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written; RV is a recreational vehicle, a camper van
A is a standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A road trip across the United States in a camper van feels like heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of IN AN RV wrap around A for America.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect peace and release, and loosely any state of supreme happiness.

clue.text: Royal Mail workers arranged mass protest

indicators.note: arranged things are put into a chosen order, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Postal employees in Britain organizing a large demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Mail is the British national postal service, so its workers include those running post offices.
explanation.definitionFit: These officials run local post offices, so they are employees of the national mail service.

clue.text: Comment concerning swindler’s victim

blocks.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a con artist's target is called a mark

explanation.surface: A note or observation about someone who has been conned.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a victim; split it into 'Comment' as definition and the rest as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a brief spoken or written observation about something.

clue.text: Product info should properly educate consumers first and foremost

indicators.note: what comes first in each word is its opening letter, so those alone are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A consumer-advice principle: labelling must above all inform buyers properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and foremost' sounds like emphasis but picks the initial letter of each of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, the detailed description of a product's technical details and features.

clue.text: European city left with nothing

blocks.note: port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship
the letter O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: A town abandoned and left empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left with nothing' reads as destitution, but 'left' is the sailor's side of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, also called Oporto, is Portugal's second city, famous for port wine.

clue.text: Remove dirty material from lists in church

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship that lists tilts to one side

explanation.surface: Purging indecent content from the parish rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like registers or rolls, but it is the verb for tilting, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash or purify something is to take away the dirt from it.

clue.text: Pine for the holiday season?

blocks.note: surface reading: to long for the festive time of year
setter's reading: a conifer, as a noun, chosen to decorate at the December festival

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the verb for yearning; read it instead as the evergreen, the kind brought indoors and decorated in December.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorated evergreen fir or pine is a centrepiece of December festivities in many homes.

clue.text: Green claims about dairy product

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or every which way, so the letters are moved

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Environmental boasts made about a milk-based product, in the spirit of greenwashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it is the anagram signal. Single cream is the British name for a thin pouring cream, close to North American light cream.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thin pouring cream with lower fat, made from milk, so it is a dairy item.

clue.text: Panic from a Liberal member

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A wave of fear spreading from a Liberal MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a member of parliament, but here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a sudden fright or anxious fear about danger.

clue.text: Denounce synopsis

blocks.note: first meaning: to criticize or disparage, as a phrasal verb
second meaning: a brief summary, usually written as one word

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings: a verb phrase for criticizing and a noun for a quick summary.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to belittle them, and a short overview of points is also called this.

clue.text: Stylish young woman wearing corduroy on vacation

indicators.note: a place on vacation is emptied out, so only the outside letters remain
whoever is wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the word emptied of its middle
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl dressed in corduroy while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like a trip away, but it means the word is vacated, leaving only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone elegant and fashionable with good taste.

clue.text: Belt and stuff to wear

blocks.note: first meaning: to hit hard, as a verb
second meaning: British slang for clothes and gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like an item of clothing, which suits 'stuff to wear', but it is the verb for striking. In British slang the answer also means one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to strike heavily; as a British slang noun it means clothing and belongings.

clue.text: Claim the lot, say, here at the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: the lot means everything
e.g. means for example, as does say
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction's close insisting the whole lot is theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the crossword stand-in for 'for example', shortened to EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something without proof is to put it forward as true, a synonym for asserting.

clue.text: Old device for extracting juice fast

blocks.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
a fruit press squeezes out juice

explanation.surface: An antique juicer that works quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one gadget, but 'fast' alone is the definition, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or delivery is a rapid one, so the adjective means speedy.

clue.text: Advanced study set up to include Virginia or another state

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: A as in A level, the advanced school exam
a den is a private room for reading or work
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Choosing between Virginia and some other state for postgraduate work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' flips the letters upwards before the insertion. 'Another state' works because Virginia, just mentioned, is a state too.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty US states, so it is a further example alongside Virginia.

clue.text: Disgusting public argument possibly following outside broadcast

indicators.note: what is following comes after, so the earlier-named piece goes second

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for an outside broadcast
to make a scene is to have a loud row in public; 'possibly' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A nasty row breaking out after a TV crew films on location.
explanation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a TV or radio programme made on location rather than in a studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something offensive to decency, repulsive or shocking.

clue.text: Appreciation of some well-chosen seats

indicators.note: some of a phrase is just a part of it, so the letters are found inside

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Gratitude for carefully picked seating at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'chosen' and the start of 'seats'.
explanation.definitionFit: As in a sense of humour or of beauty, the word means an awareness or feel for something.

clue.text: Police officer — one time — is to suffer punishment

blocks.note: cop is slang for a police officer
the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A policeman with a single offence on record facing discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop it' is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to be in trouble and receive a telling-off or penalty.

clue.text: Little bird ahead of an enormous one

indicators.note: what is ahead of something comes before it, so the pieces run in that order

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny bird standing in front of a huge one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enormous one' stands for a noun, a giant, and the contrast with 'Little' makes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods in Greek myth, so the word means a giant person or thing.

clue.text: Documentary evidence of account?

blocks.note: surface reading: papers backing up a version of events, a testimony
setter's reading: a financial account held with a lender, with its regular printed record

explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' suggests a story or report; read it as the money kind, and the paper is the monthly summary sent to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: This document from a lender lists deposits, withdrawals and balance, so it records what happened in your money holdings.

clue.text: Ruminants heading west for long grass

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: deer chew the cud, like cattle

explanation.surface: Grazing animals heading off in search of tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruminants are cud-chewing animals; the plural of the best-known short one is spelled the same as the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing in marshes and beside water.

clue.text: Man pares fresh cheese with rind

indicators.note: something fresh is newly made, so the letters are formed anew

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A man trimming a new wheel of cheese, peel and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the cheese, but it is the anagram signal; the whole clue reads as one kitchen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard Italian grating cheese is aged in large wheels with a thick, hard outer crust.
